memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: COPD with comorbid obesity and lumbar sciatica.
Symptoms and examination: Dyspnea on exertion, chronic cough, weight 95 kg, BMI 38, low back pain radiating to right leg (4/10), positive straight leg raise. On exam: reduced breath sounds bilaterally, mild expiratory wheeze, abdominal obesity, lumbar tenderness, limited lumbar flexion.
Smoking status: former smoker, 30 pack‑years, quit 2005.
Inhaler technique: Technique checked: correct for tiotropium Respimat and budesonide‑formoterol Dry Powder inhaler.
Spirometry: FEV1 1.2 L (45 % predicted), FVC 2.0 L (68 % predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.60. No prior test for change.
Assessment: COPD GOLD 2, obesity class II, sciatica likely lumbar radiculopathy.
Plan: Continue current inhalers, add pulmonary rehab referral, weight‑loss diet, continue pregabalin, diclofenac, methylcobalamin, orlistat. Review in 8 weeks.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Stable COPD, obesity unchanged, sciatica improving.
Symptoms and examination: Dyspnea on mild exertion, occasional wheeze, back pain 2/10, straight leg raise negative. Exam: vesicular breath sounds bilaterally, mild expiratory wheeze, BMI 37.8, lumbar tenderness mild.
Smoking status: former smoker, 30 pack‑years, quit 2005.
Inhaler technique: Technique checked: correct; patient using Respimat demonstrated proper slow inhalation.
Spirometry: FEV1 1.3 L (48 % predicted) ↑0.1 L from last; FVC 2.1 L (70 % predicted); FEV1/FVC 0.62.
Assessment: COPD GOLD 2, obesity class II, sciatica resolving.
Plan: Continue tiotropium OD, salbutamol SOS, budesonide‑formoterol BD. Maintain pregabalin 75 mg BD, diclofenac 50 mg BD after food, methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD. Orlistat 120 mg TID. Encourage low‑impact exercise, review in 3 months.

memories.text: Chest X‑ray (PA): Lung fields clear, no focal consolidation. Mild hyperinflation noted. Cardiac silhouette within normal limits. No pleural effusion. Impression: Consistent with COPD, no acute infection.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been feeling more short of breath when climbing stairs to the hotel’s third floor. My back pain is mostly gone, but I notice a dull ache after long shifts. I’ve been taking my inhalers as prescribed and the orlistat with meals, though I sometimes skip it when I’m busy.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: COPD stable, obesity mild improvement, sciatica resolved.
Symptoms and examination: Reports increased dyspnea on stairs, back ache mild, no radicular symptoms. Exam: breath sounds vesicular with faint wheeze, BMI 36.5, lumbar spine non‑tender, straight leg raise negative.
Smoking status: former smoker, 30 pack‑years, quit 2005.
Inhaler technique: Technique checked: correct; patient using Dry Powder inhaler demonstrated adequate inspiratory flow (>60 L/min).
Spirometry: FEV1 1.25 L (46 % predicted) ↓0.05 L from last; FVC 2.0 L (68 % predicted); FEV1/FVC 0.63.
Assessment: Slight decline in FEV1, likely due to occasional missed doses; obesity class I.
Plan: Reinforce inhaler adherence, consider short course of oral prednisolone 20 mg daily for 5 days if symptoms worsen, continue current meds, add walking program, review in 6 weeks.

memories.text:
Diagnosis: COPD stable, obesity class I, sciatica absent.
Symptoms and examination: Dyspnea on moderate exertion, occasional wheeze, weight 88 kg, BMI 32.5, no back pain. Exam: breath sounds vesicular, mild expiratory wheeze, abdominal obesity reduced, lumbar spine normal.
Smoking status: former smoker, 30 pack‑years, quit 2005.

Spirometry: FEV1 1.35 L (50 % predicted) ↑0.10 L from 2025-09-01; FVC 2.2 L (73 % predicted); FEV1/FVC 0.61.
Assessment: Improvement in lung function likely due to better inhaler adherence and weight loss.
Plan: Continue tiotropium OD, salbutamol SOS, budesonide‑formoterol BD. Maintain pregabalin 75 mg BD, diclofenac 50 mg BD after food, methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD. Orlistat 120 mg TID. Encourage maintenance of current weight, review in 4 months.
